collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks the village leader, or an elder if the game has none, and two adults)

collection.description: The one in charge must decide whether to build a second storehouse or hold a sharing feast: build, or ask for more time.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The storehouse is nearly full, and (subject) has to decide whether to build a second one or hold a great sharing feast and give the extra away. (subject.He/she) asks around. (friend) says build. (third) says share. Everyone else has a different idea again. In the end, the decision is (subject)'s, and (subject.he/she) isn't sure.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) decides to build. (subject.He/she) explains why at the fire, and admits (subject.he/she) isn't certain it's right. Some people grumble. Some people cheer. The new storehouse goes up. Is it the right choice? Ask again in ten years. (subject) is at peace with not knowing. Mostly. Some nights (subject.he/she) still wonders.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "I don't know yet," (subject) tells the village. "I'm going to think about it for a while longer." Some people are frustrated. Others seem relieved that someone in charge can say "I don't know." A week later (subject) decides on half of each: a small storehouse, and a smaller feast. Nobody's completely happy. Nobody's completely unhappy. That's often how it goes.
